intervals.label: construction and installation
intervals.quote: In July 1997, formal construction approval for ATLAS was given by CERN's Director General, starting with the calorimeters.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: From the first recorded proton-proton collisions to the LHC switch-off for Long Shutdown 3 in June 2026.

intervals.label: Phase-II upgrade (LS3)
intervals.note: Start (2026-06) is the scheduled beginning of Long Shutdown 3; the end date is the Run 4 start, itself described by the source as "currently planned" and therefore approximate/subject to change.
intervals.quote: They will all be installed and commissioned during LS3 in time for the start of Run 4, currently planned for 2029.

name: ATLAS detector
notes: CONFLICT on the overall length: the 2008 JINST detector paper says 'The dimensions of the detector are 25 m in height and 44 m in length', while atlas.cern ('46m long') and home.cern ('At 46 m long, 25 m high and 25 m wide') say 46 m. The 46 m value from the collaboration's own current page is recorded in specs.length; the 44 m JINST value is kept in the note of that quantity. The most likely explanation is that the two figures count the forward shielding differently, but no fetched source says so.

CONFLICT on the toroid field: atlas.cern's magnet page says the toroids 'provide a magnetic field of up to 3.5 Tesla' in its text and lists '4 T magnetic field on superconductor' in its barrel- and end-cap-toroid tables. 3.5 T is recorded as the delivered field and 4 T is noted as the peak on the conductor.
Trigger numbers are the 2008 design values from the JINST paper; atlas.cern's current Trigger & DAQ page quotes up to 100 000 events/s after the first level and ~1000 events/s to storage.

placements.locator: arXiv:2305.16623, abstract; 2008 JINST 3 S08003 abstract uses the same wording
placements.note: Start = 2008, when the JINST detector paper described the installation as nearing completion; year precision.
placements.quote: The ATLAS detector is installed in its experimental cavern at Point 1 of the CERN Large Hadron Collider.

calorimeters.note: Quote (official calorimeter page) supports the accordion LAr electromagnetic calorimeter at -184 C and the scintillator-tile calorimeter (about 420,000 tiles, almost 2900 tonnes); the same page lists the LAr endcap as consisting of the forward calorimeter and the electromagnetic and hadronic endcaps.
calorimeters.quote: It features a characteristic accordion structure, with a honeycomb pattern ... the calorimeter is kept at -184°C. ... about 420,000 plastic scintillator tiles working in sync. It is the heaviest part of the ATLAS experiment, weighing almost 2900 tonnes!
calorimeters.value: Liquid-argon electromagnetic calorimeter with accordion geometry kept at -184 C, scintillator-tile hadronic calorimeter of about 420 000 tiles weighing almost 2900 tonnes, and liquid-argon hadronic end-cap and forward calorimeters

diameter.locator: atlas.cern, Discover > Detector, introductory text (25 m diameter); the 2008 JINST paper gives the height as 25 m
diameter.note: atlas.cern gives '25m in diameter'; home.cern gives '25 m high and 25 m wide'. All three agree on 25 m.
diameter.quote: ATLAS has the dimensions of a cylinder, 46m long, 25m in diameter, and sits in a cavern 100m below ground.

length.note: The 2008 JINST detector paper instead states 44 m: 'The dimensions of the detector are 25 m in height and 44 m in length.' See the record notes.
length.quote: ATLAS has the dimensions of a cylinder, 46m long, 25m in diameter, and sits in a cavern 100m below ground.

muon_system.note: Quote (arXiv:2007.12539, Run-2 detector description) supports the air-core toroids and the three layers of monitored drift tubes. The trigger/precision chamber technologies in the value for the current configuration are listed on the official muon-spectrometer page: Five different detector technologies are used: Thin Gap Chambers, Resistive Plate Chambers, Monitored Drift Tubes, Small-Strip Thin-Gap Chambers and Micromegas.
muon_system.quote: to measure the deflection of muons in a magnetic field generated by the superconducting air-core toroids. ... A set of precision tracking chambers covers the region |η| < 2.7 with three layers of monitored drift tubes
muon_system.value: Air-core toroid muon spectrometer with three layers of precision tracking chambers - monitored drift tubes, plus resistive plate, thin-gap, small-strip thin-gap chambers and Micromegas for triggering

pseudorapidity_coverage.quote: tracking in the range |η| < 2.5 ... The calorimeter system covers the pseudorapidity range |η| < 4.9. Within the region |η| < 3.2, electromagnetic calorimetry ... covers the region |η| < 2.7 with three layers of monitored drift tubes ... The muon trigger system covers the range |η| < 2.4
pseudorapidity_coverage.value: Precision tracking |η| < 2.5; electromagnetic calorimetry |η| < 3.2 extended to |η| = 4.9 by the forward calorimeters; muon spectrometer |η| < 2.7 (trigger 2.4)

solenoid_field.locator: atlas.cern, Discover > Detector > Magnet System, Central Solenoid Magnet
solenoid_field.quote: It provides a 2 Tesla magnetic field in just 4.5 cm thickness.

toroid_field.note: The same page's magnet tables list '4 T magnetic field on superconductor' for the barrel and end-cap toroids.
toroid_field.quote: The ATLAS toroids use a series of eight coils to provide a magnetic field of up to 3.5 Tesla

total_mass.quote: The ATLAS detector weighs 7,000 tonnes, similar to the weight of the Eiffel Tower.

tracker.quote: Located just 3.3 cm from the LHC beam line, the Pixel Detector is the first point of detection in the ATLAS experiment.
tracker.value: Silicon pixel detector (92 million pixels, innermost layer 3.3 cm from the beam), semiconductor tracker (about 4000 modules, 6 million silicon micro-strips over 60 m²) and transition radiation tracker (300 000 thin-walled drift tubes)

trigger_rate.locator: arXiv:1110.1530 (EPJC 72 (2012) 1849), overview of the ATLAS trigger system
trigger_rate.note: Design Level-1 maximum rate (ATLAS 2010 trigger paper: "The L1 trigger system is designed to reduce the rate to a maximum of 75 kHz."). In Run 2 the L1 accept rate went up to the maximum detector read-out rate of 100 kHz and the high-level trigger recorded about 1.2 kHz on average (arXiv:2007.12539). atlas.cern Trigger-DAQ page: the second-level trigger can accept up to 100,000 events per second and selects about 1000 events per second for storage.
trigger_rate.quote: The L1 trigger system is designed to reduce the rate to a maximum of 75 kHz.

description.note: Quote is from the Run-2 detector description in arXiv:2007.12539; the official inner-detector page lists the main components as the Pixel Detector, the Semiconductor Tracker (SCT) and the Transition Radiation Tracker (TRT).
description.quote: The inner-detector system is immersed in a 2 T axial magnetic field and provides charged-particle tracking in the range |η| < 2.5. ... silicon pixel detector covers the vertex region ... It is followed by the semiconductor tracker (SCT) ... complemented by the transition radiation tracker (TRT)
description.value: Pixel detector, semiconductor tracker and transition radiation tracker inside the 2 T solenoid, reconstructing charged-particle tracks and vertices for |η| < 2.5
Accordion-geometry lead/liquid-argon sampling calorimeter measuring electron and photon energies; barrel 6.4 m long, 53 cm thick, 110 000 channels, held at -184 C

description.quote: made up of about 420,000 plastic scintillator tiles
description.value: Steel and plastic-scintillator sampling calorimeter of about 420 000 tiles and 9500 photomultipliers weighing almost 2900 tonnes, measuring hadron and jet energies in the barrel region

description.quote: 1,171 chambers with total 354,240 tubes (3 cm diameter, 0.85-6.5 m long)
description.value: Three layers of precision chambers in the air-core toroid field, including 1171 monitored-drift-tube chambers with 354 240 tubes, and wheels 25 m in diameter at each end

description.quote: At 25.3 m in length, the central toroid is the largest toroidal magnet ever constructed
description.value: Central superconducting solenoid giving 2 T in 4.5 cm of material with 38 MJ stored energy, a 25.3 m long barrel toroid of eight coils with 1.08 GJ stored, and two end-cap toroids with 0.25 GJ each

description.quote: The second-level trigger finally selects about 1000 events per second and passes them on to a data storage system for offline analysis.
description.value: Two-stage trigger selecting interesting collisions out of up to 1.7 billion per second and writing about 1000 events per second to storage, with the first-level decision taken in under 2.5 microseconds

summary.plain: A cylinder 46 metres long and 25 metres across weighing 7000 tonnes - the largest particle detector ever built. Layers of tracking chambers, calorimeters and muon chambers wrap around the point where the two proton beams meet, so that almost everything produced in a collision leaves a trace somewhere.
summary.technical: General-purpose 4π collider detector: silicon pixel + SCT + TRT inner detector in a 2 T solenoid, liquid-argon EM and forward calorimetry, scintillator-tile hadronic calorimeter, and an air-core toroid muon spectrometer. Calorimetry to |η| = 4.9, precision tracking to |η| < 2.5, muon measurement to |η| < 2.7.

technology.note: Quote is from the Run-2 detector description in arXiv:2007.12539; the same section says the muon spectrometer measures muon deflection in the field of the superconducting air-core toroids (see specs.muon_system).
technology.quote: covers nearly the entire solid angle around the collision point ... It consists of an inner tracking detector surrounded by a thin superconducting solenoid, electromagnetic and hadronic calorimeters, and a muon spectrometer incorporating three large superconducting toroidal magnets.
technology.value: General-purpose 4π collider detector with a thin superconducting solenoid around the inner-detector cavity and three large superconducting air-core toroids around the calorimeters
